title: Any onboarded provider reads every customer's Food proof snapshot, including free-text quality-incident text

request: GET https://uat.pawspace.in/api/food-proof?orderId=FOOD-VICTIM-1 with header cookie=<partner_otp platform session for provider PRV-ATTACKER-B>. Executed at both gates: lib/api-gateway.ts authorizeApiRequest and then app/api/food-proof/route.ts GET.

No row anywhere links PRV-ATTACKER-B to FOOD-VICTIM-1.
d1_after: Unchanged (read-only route). The exposure is in the response body, not the DB: the attacker now holds customer_id CUST-VICTIM-A plus the incident free text quoted above.

canonical_failure: app/api/food-proof/route.ts, GET, the final else of the scope branch: `if(scope==="customer"){requirePermission(actor,"scheduling.book");await requireCustomerOwnership(db,actor,String(order.customer_id))}else requirePermission(actor,"bookings.view");` - the non-customer branch asks for bookings.view and nothing else. bookings.view is a default service_provider permission (lib/platform-security.ts line 25), so the branch written for staff admits every onboarded provider. money_consequence: No money moves on this read. The loss is customer PII and dispute evidence: name, street address and mobile number embedded in a critical food-quality incident, plus the order's customer id, SKU and fulfilment state, handed to a competitor-provider who can use it to poach the customer or to contest/inflate a food quality claim.
blast_radius: Every food order in the platform, one orderId at a time, to any of the platform's onboarded service providers. Order ids are guessable/enumerable and are echoed back by other surfaces. Both gates allow, so there is no compensating control.
regression: tests/ptja-w2b-crm-media-authz.test.mjs :: "W2B-M01: a provider session cannot read another customer's food proof" + "W2B-M01: staff still read the food proof"
fix_note: The non-customer branch is gated on customers.view instead of bookings.view. The four sibling proof routes bind the caller with requireProviderOwnership, but food orders carry no provider column to bind to, so the gate is the capability the platform already defines for reading customer records - held by founder/superuser/admin/manager/associate and not by service_provider. Same correction as the funeral-memorial and relocation routes.

repeatable: yes - run twice in two fresh in-memory databases (run1, run2); identical 200/200/200/200 and identical DB rows both times. The walking control also refused identically on both runs.

AND booking_id=?").bind(id,order.id).first<Row>();if(!media)throw ...;if(String(media.access_status)!=="quarantined"||String(media.scan_status)!=="pending")throw ...` - there is no `if(String(media.created_by)===input.actorId)` refusal. title: REFUTATION: the voice provider callback does NOT act on an unsigned, wrongly-signed, stale or replayed payload, and an absent secret refuses rather than unlocks
actor: anonymous caller (the route is gateway-allowlisted at lib/api-gateway.ts line 14, so no session is presented)
request: Five POSTs to https://uat.pawspace.in/api/voice-provider-webhook with body {"CallSid":"SIMCALL-1","CustomField":"VCALL-1","CallStatus":"completed","EventType":"terminal","ConversationDuration":42} against a seeded voice_call_orders row VCALL-1 in state 'dialing': (1) no signature headers; (2) x-pawspace-voice-signature=deadbeef*8 with a fresh timestamp; (3) a correct HMAC-SHA256 over `${timestamp}.${rawBody}`; (4) the byte-identical signed request replayed; (5) a correct HMAC over a timestamp 600000 ms old. Plus a separate world with NO PAWSPACE_VOICE_*/EXOTEL_* variables set at all, sent both an HMAC computed with the empty secret and HTTP Basic. Boundary stubbed: the telephony transport is PAWSPACE_VOICE_TRANSPORT=local_simulator_non_production with a scratch PAWSPACE_VOICE_SIMULATOR_SECRET, so no outbound network call is made; signature verification, dedup and the state machine are the real code paths.
response: (1) 401 {"error":"No webhook signature or Basic credentials presented"}. (2) 401 {"error":"Signature does not match"}. (3) 200 {"ok":true,"applied":true,"stateChanged":true,"from":"dialing","to":"completed","inferred":"connected","eventId":"local_simulator_non_production:SIMCALL-1:terminal"}. (4) 200 {"ok":true,"duplicate":true,"applied":false,"reason":"Provider event already processed"} - answered 200 so the carrier stops retrying, but applied=false. (5) 401 {"error":"Signature timestamp is outside the freshness window"}. Unconfigured world: both requests 401 {"error":"Telephony provider is not connected"}.
d1_after: After all five requests: voice_call_provider_events holds exactly ONE row - {"provider_event_id":"local_simulator_non_production:SIMCALL-1:terminal","event_kind":"completed","applied":1,"signature_mechanism":"hmac"}. voice_call_orders.state = 'completed' after the first valid request and STILL 'completed' after the replay - the replay applied nothing. The four rejected requests wrote no row at all.
repeatable: yes - both scripts run twice in fresh in-memory databases; byte-identical statuses, bodies and DB state every time
canonical_failure: NOT A DEFECT. lib/voice-telephony-provider.ts line 115 `if (!secret) return { verified: false, mechanism: null, reason: "Webhook secret is not configured" };` makes an absent secret refuse; line 121 enforces the 300000 ms freshness window; lib/voice-outbound-governance.ts line 644 `if (!verification.verified) return { accepted:false, status:401, ... }` returns before any write; line 662 `INSERT OR IGNORE ... voice_call_provider_events` on the composed provider_event_id, plus line 664 `if(!Number(insert.meta.changes)) return {...duplicate:true, applied:false}`, is what makes the replay inert. lib/voice-telephony-provider.ts line 328-330 selectTelephonyProvider falls through to `disconnectedTelephony`, whose verifyWebhook is hardcoded `{verified:false}` (line 83), when credentials are absent.
money_consequence: None. This was the hypothesis that a carrier callback could advance a call to 'completed'/'connected' - and thereby the billing and disposition record - without a credential or by replay. It does not.
blast_radius: None. Recorded so the next sweep does not re-litigate this endpoint.

title: One staff actor mints a clean, non-synthetic service-proof asset whose storage reference is an attacker-supplied public URL, and the platform's service-proof gate accepts it
actor: single staff identity ops.manager@pawspace.test, role=manager. No second person, no upload grant, no bytes, no scanner.
response:
1) 201 {"data":{"id":"MEDIA-FEBC789A-E2F","ref":"media://asset/MEDIA-FEBC789A-E2F","purpose":"after_service","scanStatus":"pending","accessStatus":"pending_upload","synthetic":false,"storage":{"mode":"not_connected","uploadReady":false}}}
2) 200 {"data":{"scanStatus":"pending","accessStatus":"quarantined","proofReady":false}} - the public URL was accepted verbatim as the storage reference
3) 200 {"data":{"scanStatus":"clean","accessStatus":"ready","proofReady":true}} - self-approved by the same actor who created it
assertServiceProofRef: ACCEPTED (returned without throwing).
EXECUTED CONTROL on the sibling lib (lib/walking-proof-governance.ts, evidence p02b-walking-control.mjs): prepare_media issues an HMAC'd single-use upload grant token; the same public URL passed as storageObjectId is REFUSED 400 "Storage confirmation must use an opaque object ID, not a public URL"; and record_media_scan by the submitting actor is REFUSED 403 "Dog Walking proof cannot be scan-approved by the actor who submitted it". Both runs.
d1_after: service_media_assets: [{"id":"MEDIA-FEBC789A-E2F","booking_id":"BK-GROOM-1","provider_id":"PRV-GROOMER-1","purpose":"after_service","storage_key":"https://attacker.example.test/not-a-storage-object.jpg","scan_status":"clean","access_status":"ready","retention_status":"active","synthetic":0,"created_by":"ops.manager@pawspace.test"}]. service_media_events: three rows - upload_prepared, upload_confirmed, scan_passed - all actor_id=ops.manager@pawspace.test.
repeatable: yes - run twice in two fresh in-memory databases; identical 201/200/200, identical DB rows, and assertServiceProofRef ACCEPTED both times
canonical_failure: app/api/service-media/route.ts PATCH. Three separate omissions in one handler: (a) `if(input.action==="confirm_upload"){requirePermission(actor,"bookings.manage");if(!input.storageReference?.trim())return json({error:"Verified storage reference is required"},400); ... const storageKey=input.storageReference.trim();` - the only validation is non-empty, so any string including a public URL becomes the storage key; the sibling libs reject `objectId.includes("://")`. (b) there is no upload grant/token at all in this route - service-media POST returns `storage:{mode:"not_connected",uploadReady:false}` and nothing binds the later confirm_upload to a single-use secret, where lib/walking-proof-governance.ts and lib/food-proof-governance.ts both issue an HMAC'd grant and verify `String(grant.token_hash)!==await digest(token)`. (c) `if(input.action==="record_scan"){requirePermission(actor,"bookings.manage"); ...}` has no `if(String(asset.created_by)===actor.email)` refusal, so the creator approves their own asset. The resulting row then passes every clause of assertServiceProofRef in lib/service-media-security.ts, which checks booking, provider, purpose, scan_status='clean', access_status='ready', retention_status='active' and synthetic=0 - all of which this fabricated row satisfies.
money_consequence: assertServiceProofRef is the gate the platform uses to decide whether a service was actually performed (its only callers are the grooming completion path in app/api/grooming-lifecycle/route.ts lines 57 and 68, where before/after photo proof is mandatory before a job may be completed). A single operator can therefore mark a grooming job complete - releasing the customer charge and the provider's completion-linked payout - with proof that is one row and a URL string, no image and no scan. It also works in reverse as false evidence in a customer dispute. The storage_key being an arbitrary external URL means the 'proof' anyone later opens is a page the person who wrote the record controls.
blast_radius: Every booking that has a provider_work_orders row - the route's only precondition - for every holder of bookings.manage (founder, superuser, admin, manager). Both proof purposes (before_service and after_service) and every service that uses provider_work_orders. Note the same actor also passes the POST step's requireProviderOwnership, because actorManagesProviders() in lib/server-auth.ts line 98 returns true on bookings.manage, so no provider relationship is needed either.
status: PARTIALLY FIXED — public-URL proof closed; upload-grant parity carried forward
regression: tests/ptja-w2b-service-media.test.mjs :: "W2B-M04: a public URL cannot become a service-proof storage reference" + "W2B-M04: an opaque storage object id is still accepted"
fix_note: confirm_upload now applies the sibling libraries' exact rule - objectId.includes("://") || !/^[A-Za-z0-9._\/-]{8,256}$/ -> 400 'Storage confirmation must use an opaque object ID, not a public URL'. The proof anyone opens can no longer be a URL the writer controls.
carried_forward: NOT closed: this route issues no upload grant at all (its POST returns storage:{mode:'not_connected'}), where lib/walking-proof-governance.ts and lib/food-proof-governance.ts mint an HMAC'd single-use token and verify it on confirmation. Building that flow is a design decision about how this route obtains storage, not a missing check, so it is recorded with those two libraries named as the reference implementation. Also carried: the same actor can create an asset and record its clean scan - checked, and the sibling libs do NOT enforce actor separation either, so that is a platform-wide maker/checker question rather than a defect unique to this route.

title: An unrecognised PATCH action on service-media falls through to REVOKE, irreversibly destroying an approved proof asset and logging it as a deliberate operator revocation
actor: staff ops.manager@pawspace.test, role=manager (bookings.manage) - i.e. the normal operator of this console, with no hostile intent required
request: Against an already-approved before_service proof asset MEDIA-B5E4B813-EB5 (scan_status=clean, access_status=ready, retention_status=active) for booking BK-GROOM-1: PATCH https://uat.pawspace.in/api/service-media with staff headers and body {"id":"MEDIA-B5E4B813-EB5","action":"record_scann","scanResult":"clean"} - one letter different from the real action name. Then two attempts to restore it through the same route: PATCH {action:"confirm_upload",storageReference:"grooming/object/abcdefgh"} and PATCH {action:"record_scan",scanResult:"clean"}.
response: Unknown action: 200 {"data":{"id":"MEDIA-B5E4B813-EB5","accessStatus":"revoked","retentionStatus":"revoked","proofReady":false}} - no error, no mention that the action was not understood. Restore attempt 1: 409 {"error":"Media upload is not awaiting storage confirmation"}. Restore attempt 2: 409 {"error":"Media asset is not awaiting scan review"}. The proof gate afterwards: assertServiceProofRef REJECTED, Response 409 "Service media asset upload is not ready for service proof".
d1_before: service_media_assets: {"id":"MEDIA-B5E4B813-EB5","scan_status":"clean","access_status":"ready","retention_status":"active"}. service_media_events: three rows - upload_prepared, upload_confirmed, scan_passed.
d1_after: service_media_assets: {"id":"MEDIA-B5E4B813-EB5","scan_status":"clean","access_status":"revoked","retention_status":"revoked"} - and still exactly that after both restore attempts; this route offers no path back. service_media_events gained {"event_type":"media_revoked","actor_id":"ops.manager@pawspace.test","detail_json":"{\"reason\":\"Revoked by authorized operator\"}"} - the audit trail asserts a deliberate revocation the operator never requested. A security_audit_events row service_media.revoke is written alongside it.
repeatable: yes - run twice in two fresh in-memory databases; identical 200-then-revoked, identical 409/409 on restore, identical proof-gate rejection, identical event rows
canonical_failure: app/api/service-media/route.ts, PATCH. The handler dispatches with two `if` blocks and then an unguarded tail: after `if(input.action==="confirm_upload"){...}` and `if(input.action==="record_scan"){...}` the very next statement is `requirePermission(actor,"bookings.manage");await db.prepare("UPDATE service_media_assets SET access_status='revoked',retention_status='revoked',updated_at=? WHERE id=?")...` with no `if(input.action==="revoke")` and no final `return json({error:"Unsupported action"},400)`. The declared type `MediaActionInput.action:"confirm_upload"|"record_scan"|"revoke"` is compile-time only and the route never validates the runtime value, even though the same file validates purpose and MIME against explicit Sets on POST (allowedPurpose, allowedMime). Every sibling proof route ends its action dispatch with an explicit refusal instead - e.g. app/api/walking-proof/route.ts `else return json({error:"Unsupported Dog Walking proof action"},400)`.
money_consequence: The revoked asset can no longer satisfy assertServiceProofRef, which is the mandatory before/after photo gate on grooming completion (app/api/grooming-lifecycle/route.ts lines 57 and 68). Destroying the proof blocks the job being completed - so the customer charge and the provider's completion-linked payout stall - and in a dispute the evidence is gone with an audit trail that says an operator chose to destroy it. Because it is a silent 200 on a typo, this fires by accident, not only by attack.
blast_radius: Every service_media_assets row, for every holder of bookings.manage, via any misspelled/renamed/older-client action string. There is no id-to-booking or id-to-provider ownership check on this branch either, so any asset id on the platform can be revoked by id alone. No restore exists on this surface.
regression: tests/ptja-w2b-service-media.test.mjs :: "W2B-M05: a misspelled action does not revoke the asset" + "W2B-M05: an explicit revoke still revokes"
fix_note: The unguarded revoke tail now requires action==='revoke' and refuses anything else with a 400. The declared TypeScript union already said the action is one of three values; this enforces it at runtime instead of only at compile time. Revocation itself is unchanged.

title: REFUTATION: a proof asset from one walking booking is NOT accepted as proof for another, nor in another purpose slot, and a provider cannot read a booking they are not assigned to
domain: service media & proof-of-service (walking-proof, the pattern shared by sitting/taxi/boarding)

title: A request-body boolean turns off the 21:00-09:00 IST quiet-hours bar on bulk outbound voice campaigns, and the security audit record does not say it was used
response:
(a) 201 {"data":{"connected":true,"dialled":0,"audience":0,"reason":"Quiet hours (21:00-09:00 IST): no outbound calls placed. Pass force to override for an urgent callback."}} - refused at the gate, returned BEFORE buildOutboundAudience.
(b) 201 {"data":{"connected":true,"campaign":"new_lead_followup","dialled":0,"skipped":0,"failed":0,"audience":0,"calls":[]}} - no quiet-hours reason at all: the gate was passed and execution continued into the dial loop. Also measured: the gateway maps this path to the fail-open fallback permission dashboard.view, not marketing.manage - only the route's own requirePermission(actor,"marketing.manage") holds that line.
d1_before: security_audit_events: no haptik_outbound.trigger row. haptik_outbound_calls: 0 rows.
repeatable: yes - run twice in two fresh in-memory databases with the same stubbed clock; identical bodies and identical audit rows both times
canonical_failure: lib/haptik-outbound-governance.ts line 96: `if (!input.force && isQuietHours(at)) return { ...base, connected: true, reason: "Quiet hours (21:00-09:00 IST): no outbound calls placed. Pass force to override for an urgent callback." };` - the guard is conjoined with a caller-controlled boolean that arrives from the request body via app/api/haptik-outbound/route.ts POST `force:Boolean(body.force)`. Nothing bounds what force may cover: the same call proceeds to a loop over an audience of up to `limit`, which buildOutboundAudience clamps at 5000. The audit call two lines later in the route, `securityAudit(db,actor,"haptik_outbound.trigger","haptik_outbound",campaign,...,{campaign,dialled,skipped,failed,audience,reason})`, does not include force, and neither the haptik_outbound_calls row nor its context_json records an override. Contrast lib/voice-call-gate.ts, whose header states the opposite rule for the other automated-dialling surface: 'ONLY the worker environment is consulted. There is no request header, query parameter, cookie or request-body field anywhere in this module - a browser cannot turn voice on, in any environment.'
money_consequence: No money moves directly. The exposure is regulatory and reputational: up to 5000 automated marketing voice calls placed to Indian consumer numbers between 21:00 and 09:00 IST on one request, with an audit trail that cannot afterwards distinguish that run from a compliant daytime one. The stated justification in the code is 'an urgent callback' (singular); the parameter is applied to the whole campaign.
blast_radius: Every outbound campaign (new_lead_followup, reactivation, subscription_pitch) and every contact in its audience, up to the 5000 clamp per request, for any holder of marketing.manage (founder, superuser, admin). Consent/opt-out filtering and the 7-day frequency cap are NOT bypassed by force - only the quiet-hours bar is.
status: PARTIALLY FIXED — override now audited; its scope is a compliance decision
fix_note: The security audit record now carries quietHoursOverride, so a campaign dialled through the 21:00-09:00 IST bar is no longer indistinguishable in the trail from one dialled at noon.
carried_forward: NOT changed: that a caller-supplied boolean can lift the quiet-hours bar for a BULK run at all. The code's own refusal describes force as an override 'for an urgent callback' - singular - while the same call proceeds over an audience of up to the 5000 clamp. Choosing what force may legitimately cover (one contact? a named recipient? a capped batch?) is a marketing/compliance decision, and picking a bound would be inventing policy. RECOMMENDED for the owner: bound force to a single named recipient, or to a small explicit cap, and keep the audit field. Note also that consent/opt-out filtering and the 7-day frequency cap are NOT bypassed by force - only the quiet-hours bar is.

title: The WhatsApp webhook trusts a caller-supplied customerId and silently discards the contradicting phone: a message from one customer's number is filed on another customer's canonical thread, stamped 'canonical_customer_id', and opens that customer's 24-hour outbound session window
actor: any holder of PAWSPACE_WHATSAPP_UAT_WEBHOOK_SECRET - i.e. the WhatsApp BSP/provider integration, not the customer. The request is correctly HMAC-signed; the signature is what authenticates the CHANNEL, and it is then treated as if it authenticated the SUBJECT.
request: POST https://uat.pawspace.in/api/whatsapp-uat-webhook, headers {x-pawspace-signature: <valid HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body>, x-pawspace-event-id: evt-run1, x-pawspace-whatsapp-provider: sandbox_simulator}, body {"type":"inbound_message","customerId":"CUST-VICTIM-A","phone":"+919800000999","text":"Please confirm the refund to my new account"}. +919800000999 is the primary_phone of a DIFFERENT canonical customer, CUST-ATTACKER-Z; CUST-VICTIM-A's primary_phone is +919800000001. Boundary stubbed: PAWSPACE_WHATSAPP_ENV=uat and a scratch webhook secret in the worker env, and the sandbox_simulator provider - nothing leaves the process.
response: 201 {"ok":true,"environment":"uat","externalDelivery":false,"data":{"messageId":"MSG-WA-77E8B4D0-E24","threadId":"THREAD-BC19C040-7EC","customerId":"CUST-VICTIM-A","status":"received","identitySource":"canonical_customer_id"},"orchestrator":{"outcome":"handoff","handoffReason":"refund_payment_dispute","autonomousExecution":false}} - the platform reports the identity as canonically resolved, and escalates a refund dispute to a human on the victim's thread.
d1_before: canonical_customers: CUST-VICTIM-A (+919800000001) and CUST-ATTACKER-Z (+919800000999). communication_threads: empty. communication_messages: empty. whatsapp_uat_sessions: empty. whatsapp_uat_identity_reviews: empty.
d1_after: communication_threads: [{"id":"THREAD-BC19C040-7EC","customer_id":"CUST-VICTIM-A","status":"open"}]. communication_messages: [{"id":"MSG-WA-77E8B4D0-E24","customer_id":"CUST-VICTIM-A","direction":"inbound","channel":"whatsapp","payload_json":"{\"text\":\"Please confirm the refund to my new account\",...}","policy_json":"{...,\"identitySource\":\"canonical_customer_id\",\"signatureRequired\":true,\"sessionWindowHours\":24}"}] - the phone +919800000999 appears NOWHERE on the record. whatsapp_uat_events: one row, customer_id=CUST-VICTIM-A. whatsapp_uat_sessions: [{"customer_id":"CUST-VICTIM-A","provider":"sandbox_simulator","last_inbound_at":1787690324464}] - the 24-hour free-form window is now OPEN for the victim. whatsapp_uat_identity_reviews: STILL EMPTY - no governed identity review was raised.
repeatable: yes - run twice in two fresh in-memory databases; identical 201, identical identitySource, identical session row, empty identity-review table both times
canonical_failure: lib/whatsapp-uat-adapter.ts line 30, in resolveWhatsAppUatCustomer: `if(input.customerId)return{customerId:await canonicalCustomer(db,text(input.customerId)),identitySource:"canonical_customer_id" as const};` - canonicalCustomer only checks the id EXISTS; input.providerIdentity is never compared with it and is then dropped. The strict path is the very next lines (31-35), which resolve by phone, require exactly one canonical_customers match, and otherwise open a whatsapp_uat_identity_reviews row and throw Response 409 'WhatsApp identity requires governed customer resolution' - so the whole identity check runs only when the OPTIONAL customerId is absent. app/api/whatsapp-uat-webhook/route.ts passes both fields through verbatim: `const customerId=String(payload.customerId||"").trim()||null,providerIdentity=String(payload.phone||payload.providerIdentity||"").trim()||null`. The downstream effect on the outbound window is lib/whatsapp-uat-adapter.ts queueWhatsAppUatOutbound: `withinSession=Boolean(session&&now-Number(session.last_inbound_at||0)<=24*60*60_000)` and `if(!withinSession){const key=text(input.templateKey);if(!key)return{...reason:"approved_template_required_outside_session"}}` - an inbound event forged this way removes the approved-template requirement for that customer for 24 hours.
money_consequence: The AI orchestrator classified the injected text as refund_payment_dispute and queued a human handoff on the victim's thread - a CX agent now sees 'Please confirm the refund to my new account' as words from that customer, on a conversation the platform's own record labels canonically identified. That is a payment-redirection social-engineering primitive aimed at staff, with the platform vouching for the identity. Separately, the opened 24-hour session window removes the approved-template constraint on outbound WhatsApp to that customer.
blast_radius: Any canonical customer, by id, on any signed inbound event - so the whole customer base is reachable by whoever holds the webhook secret (the messaging vendor, anyone who obtains the secret from it, or any misconfigured route to it). The phone field, the one datum that could contradict the claim, is silently discarded rather than being made to agree.
regression: tests/ptja-w2b-crm-media-authz.test.mjs :: "W2B-M07: a claimed customerId that contradicts the sending phone is refused" + "W2B-M07: an agreeing claim, and a phone-only message, both still resolve"
fix_note: A claimed customerId must now AGREE with the phone the message came from; a contradiction opens the same whatsapp_uat_identity_reviews row the strict path already uses and refuses 409, rather than the claim silently winning. The phone is the one datum the sender demonstrably controls at the transport level and it was being dropped. A claim with no phone beside it, and a phone with no claim, both behave exactly as before.

title: REFUTATION: taxi-proof's missing `if(!booking)` guard is not a crash or an auth bypass - getTaxiBooking throws a 404 Response, so the route answers 404, not 500
actor: staff ops.admin@pawspace.test (role=admin) and a partner_otp platform session for PRV-B, both against a booking id that does not exist
request: app/api/taxi-proof/route.ts is the only one of the five proof routes whose GET and POST do NOT null-check the booking - `const booking=await getTaxiBooking(db,bookingId)` is followed straight by `String(booking.customer_id)` / `String(booking.provider_id)`, where walking-proof, sitting-proof and boarding-proof all have `if(!booking)return json({error:"... not found"},404)`. Four executions against a fully-populated schema (ensureTaxiProofTables + ensureTaxiOpsTables + ensureCanonicalBookingReadModel, so the lookup itself works and simply finds nothing): GET /api/taxi-proof?bookingId=DOES-NOT-EXIST as staff; the same as a provider session; GET ?scope=customer&bookingId=DOES-NOT-EXIST as staff; POST {"bookingId":"DOES-NOT-EXIST","action":"prepare_media","idempotencyKey":"t-run1"} as a provider session. Plus a direct call to getTaxiBooking(db,"DOES-NOT-EXIST") and the walking-proof equivalent as a control.
response: getTaxiBooking(db,"DOES-NOT-EXIST") THREW a Response with status 404 and body "Canonical Pet Taxi booking not found" - it never returns null, so `booking.customer_id` is never evaluated. All four route calls: 404, body {"error":"Unable to load Pet Taxi proof records"} (GET) / {"error":"Unable to update Pet Taxi proof records"} (POST) - the status is preserved and the body redacted by authError() in lib/server-auth.ts because the thrown Response is an ungoverned client error. Control: walking-proof returned 404 {"error":"Dog Walking booking not found"}.
d1_before: taxi_trips, canonical_bookings, service_media_assets, taxi_proof_action_keys: all empty.
d1_after: Unchanged - no taxi_proof_action_keys row, no service_media_assets row, no phantom records for the non-existent booking id, on any of the four calls.
repeatable: yes - run twice in two fresh in-memory databases; identical 404s and identical empty tables both times
canonical_failure: NOT A DEFECT, though the two routes differ in message quality. lib/taxi-lifecycle.ts getTaxiBooking throws `new Response("Canonical Pet Taxi booking not found",{status:404})` rather than returning null, which is why the absent guard in app/api/taxi-proof/route.ts is inert. The only observable difference from its siblings is that the 404 body is the generic redacted string instead of the specific 'not found' message, because the thrown Response is not marked via markGovernedHttpError - a diagnostics nit, not a security or state defect.
money_consequence: None. This was the hypothesis that the missing null check produces a 500 or lets a staff proof action write records against a booking that does not exist. Neither happens.

title: REFUTATION: the anonymous AI web-chat lead capture does NOT feed the automated outbound voice dialler - ai_web_leads is a terminal table with no consumer
actor: fully anonymous caller - no session cookie, no staff headers, no identity of any kind
request: POST https://uat.pawspace.in/api/ai-web-chat with NO auth headers and body {"mode":"public","sessionKey":"sess-run1","message":"call me about grooming","name":"Anon","phone":"+919812345678","email":"anon@example.test"}, executed at both gates; then buildOutboundAudience(db,{campaign}) run directly for all three campaigns (new_lead_followup, reactivation, subscription_pitch), and row counts taken on lead_work_items and crm_contacts.
response: GATEWAY: ALLOW with permission=null and a public actor {"email":"","roleCode":"public","permissions":[]} - the path is deliberately allowlisted for mode!=='authenticated' (lib/api-gateway.ts lines 49-53). HANDLER: 201 {"data":{"mode":"public","lead":{"captured":true,"sessionKey":"sess-run1","customerDataAccess":false},"customerDataAccess":false,"toolExecution":false}}. buildOutboundAudience returned [] for all three campaigns.
d1_after: ai_web_leads: [{"id":"AIWEBLEAD-2182BD6A-01B","session_key":"sess-run1","name":"Anon","phone":"+919812345678","email":"anon@example.test","status":"new"}]. lead_work_items: 0 rows. crm_contacts: 0 rows. All three outbound audiences still empty.
repeatable: yes - run twice in two fresh in-memory databases; identical 201, identical single ai_web_leads row, identical zero counts and empty audiences
canonical_failure: NOT A DEFECT. lib/ai-web-chat-adapter.ts captureAiWebLead writes only `INSERT INTO ai_web_leads ... ON CONFLICT(session_key) DO UPDATE` - it touches no CRM table. lib/haptik-outbound-governance.ts buildOutboundAudience reads exclusively from lead_work_items JOIN crm_contacts (and the subscription/booking tables for the other two campaigns), never ai_web_leads. A repo-wide search for `ai_web_leads` outside lib/ai-web-chat-adapter.ts returns nothing at all: no route reads it, no sweep promotes it. The per-sessionKey upsert also bounds repeat submissions on one key to a single row.
money_consequence: None. The hypothesis under test was a chain: anonymous unauthenticated lead injection -> the lead lands in an outbound campaign audience -> triggerOutboundCampaign places automated voice calls to attacker-chosen numbers (toll/harassment abuse using the platform's caller ID). The chain is broken at the first hop. What remains is unauthenticated, uncaptcha'd insert growth in ai_web_leads keyed by a caller-chosen sessionKey - storage noise with no downstream consumer, not a dialling primitive.
